record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: Find a (2n+1)-dimensional variety S inside H^n = R^(4n) for which the local cohomology of the sheaf R of Cauchy-Fueter regular functions with support in S vanishes in every degree j different from 2n-1 and is nonzero in degree 2n-1. This is intended as a quaternionic analogue of the classical pure n-codimensionality theorem for R^n inside C^n with respect to the sheaf O of holomorphic functions.

evidence.quote: Problem: Find a (2n+1)-dimensional variety S in H^n=R^(4n) such that H_S^j(H^n,R)=0 for all j not equal to 2n-1.
we need to prove a quaternionic analog of the classical theorem on the pure n-codimensionality of R^n in C^n, with respect to O.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^n \cong \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ denote the space of $n$-tuples of quaternions, and let $\mathcal{R}$ be the sheaf on $\mathbb{H}^n$ of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions, i.e. functions $f:\mathbb{H}^n\to\mathbb{H}$ that are annihilated coordinate-wise by the Cauchy–Fueter operator $\partial_{\bar q_i}=\partial_{x_i^0}+i\,\partial_{x_i^1}+j\,\partial_{x_i^2}+k\,\partial_{x_i^3}$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. For a closed subset $S\subset\mathbb{H}^n$, let $\mathcal{H}^j_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R})$ denote the $j$-th local cohomology of $\mathcal{R}$ with support in $S$.

Construct a real-analytic (or semi-analytic) subvariety $S\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ of real dimension $2n+1$ such that
$$\mathcal{H}^j_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R}) = 0 \quad \text{for all } j\neq 2n-1, \qquad \mathcal{H}^{2n-1}_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R}) \neq 0.$$

This is the quaternionic analogue of the classical purity result stating that $\mathbb{R}^n\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is purely $n$-codimensional with respect to the sheaf $\mathcal{O}$ of holomorphic functions.
artifact.status_search_result: The case $n=2$ (i.e. 5-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^2$) has been addressed by Colombo–Damiano–Sabadini–Struppa, who constructed quaternionic hyperfunctions on certain 5-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^2$ realizing the expected pure codimensionality with respect to $\mathcal{R}$. The general case for arbitrary $n$ — producing $(2n+1)$-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^n$ with local cohomology concentrated in degree $2n-1$ — does not appear to have a complete published resolution.

status_evidence.title: Quaternionic hyperfunctions on five-dimensional varieties in H^2
status_evidence.snippet: One can define quaternionic hyperfunctions on (2n+1)-dimensional real varieties in H^n; the n=2 case is treated here.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is solved for n=2 by constructing quaternionic hyperfunctions as boundary values of regular functions on 5-dimensional varieties in H^2.

status_evidence.title: Regular functions of several quaternionic variables and the Cauchy-Fueter complex
status_evidence.snippet: Cohomology of any open set in H^n with coefficients in R vanishes in degree at least 2n-1, related to the dimension of the characteristic variety of the Cauchy-Fueter system.
status_evidence.claim: The relevant cohomological degree 2n-1 is identified, motivating the purity question.
